site.tagline: Computer Engineering graduate · K. N. Toosi University of Technology
about: I hold a BSc in Computer Engineering from K. N. Toosi University of Technology (GPA 18.37 / 20) and am applying for a Master's degree in Germany.

My work moves between artificial intelligence and software: a thesis on sentiment analysis of YouTube comments, an offline app for reading German books and films, and full-stack systems. As Head Teaching Assistant at Sejong University, I led six TAs producing machine-learning course material.

projects.title: YouTube Comment Sentiment Analysis
projects.summary: How far can lightweight classifiers get against a large transformer? Classic models improved with lexicon features and weak supervision, plus an app that analyses any video's comments.
projects.course: BSc thesis, K. N. Toosi University of Technology
projects.overview: Three-class sentiment analysis (positive, neutral, negative) of social-media comments. Transformer models are accurate but heavy; the thesis asks how close cheap classic models can come, and which kind of extra data helps them most.
did: Built a preprocessing pipeline: URL and mention normalisation, emojis converted to text, lemmatisation, and VADER sentiment-lexicon features.
Collected extra YouTube comments with the YouTube Data API v3 and pseudo-labelled them with Twitter-RoBERTa (weak supervision). Also tested paraphrase-based augmentation with Gemma 3.
Trained Logistic Regression and Linear SVM classifiers with the added VADER features and weakly supervised data.

Built a Streamlit app that fetches up to 5,000 comments from a video or reads a CSV, runs several models side by side, and shows sentiment charts, agreement with RoBERTa and confusion matrices. A hybrid mode uses the fast model and only falls back to RoBERTa when its confidence is low.
results: Macro F1 rose from 66.4% (Logistic Regression) and 65.1% (Linear SVM) to about 72.2%.
Weak supervision helped more than paraphrase augmentation.
Reference point: Twitter-RoBERTa reaches 88.9% macro F1 on the same task.

projects.title: ChamFlick DE
projects.summary: An offline Android app for learning German from real books and films: tap any word for meaning, grammar and pronunciation, with every noun coloured by its gender.
projects.overview: Reading German books and watching German films is the best practice, but constant dictionary look-ups break the flow. ChamFlick puts the dictionary inside the page and the subtitles.
did: Tap any word in a PDF, EPUB, scanned page or live film subtitle to open a dictionary card with its meaning, grammar and pronunciation. Scanned books are read with OCR.

Every noun is coloured by gender (der / die / das / plural) in text and subtitles. A sentence parser resolves ambiguous words such as Band or Messer, and nouns it is unsure about stay uncoloured instead of being guessed.
German-specific look-ups: separable verbs are rejoined (in “fügte … hinzu”, a tap on fügte opens hinzufügen) and compound words are split (Apfelbaum → Apfel + Baum).
Everything runs on the phone: no account and no internet connection.

projects.title: Rahi: Bus Ticket Reservation System
projects.summary: A bilingual (English / Persian) bus booking site with a Go API that can never sell the same seat twice. Built in 2024, reworked in 2026.
projects.overview: A practice project modelled on Safar724, an Iranian intercity bus booking site: search trips, pick seats on a drawing of the bus, enter passengers and receive a ticket. It is not affiliated with Safar724 and the payment page is a demo.
did: Layered Go REST API (Gin, GORM) on PostgreSQL with numbered SQL migrations; web, service and store layers that each only know the layer below.

No double sales: each booking runs in one transaction that locks the chosen seat rows in a fixed order (SELECT … FOR UPDATE) so bookings cannot deadlock, and a partial unique index makes the database itself refuse a second sale.
Seats are held for 10 minutes while the buyer reviews and pays, and released if they do not.

React + TypeScript frontend: search state in the URL, city autocomplete over 915 cities, seat maps drawn from each bus type's floor plan, and English (left-to-right) and Persian (right-to-left) with Persian digits and calendar. Checked at 360–480 px phone widths.
GitHub Actions CI and Docker Compose for the local database.
results: Concurrency tests against a real PostgreSQL: 20 buyers request the same seat at the same moment and exactly one gets it.
24 buyers with overlapping seat choices all finish without a deadlock.

projects.title: Asphalt Crack Segmentation
projects.summary: Pixel-level crack detection with a U-Net built from scratch, trained on asphalt photos I took and labelled myself.
projects.overview: Finding thin cracks in road surfaces, pixel by pixel: for every pixel, decide whether it belongs to a crack.
did: Photographed cracked asphalt and labelled the cracks myself as polygon masks in COCO format.
Built a U-Net-style network in PyTorch: four encoder levels, a bottleneck and four decoder levels joined by skip connections.
Wrote a balanced 70 / 15 / 15 train / validation / test split, the training loop, and an evaluation that reports IoU and draws the predicted cracks over the photos.
Fought overfitting with augmentation that rotates and scales each photo together with its crack outlines, and with a dropout-regularised version of the network.
results: Thin cracks are a hard target for IoU: a prediction a few pixels off to the side already loses most of its overlap.
With a small hand-labelled dataset the network overfits quickly; augmentation and dropout help, but the size and quality of the data matter most.

projects.title: Omegle Clone
projects.summary: Real-time anonymous text and video chat: random partner matching, rooms joinable by ID, and peer-to-peer video over WebRTC.
projects.overview: A full-stack clone of Omegle-style random chat, built as the Internet Engineering course project.
did: Node.js and Express backend following MVC (models, controllers, routes, views), with PostgreSQL through the Sequelize ORM for users, meetings, participants and messages.
Socket.IO for signalling and text chat; WebRTC for peer-to-peer video between matched users.
Random partner matching, meeting rooms joinable by ID, an option to hide the camera, and a layout that works on phones.
Served over HTTPS with locally trusted certificates, since browsers only allow camera access on secure origins, and packaged with Docker Compose.

projects.title: 8-bit Processor in Verilog
projects.summary: A small accumulator-based CPU with a hard-wired control unit, designed register by register and simulated in ModelSim.
projects.overview: Designing a working processor from the registers up, in the style of Mano's basic computer.
did: Registers AR and PC (5-bit) and DR, AC, IR, TR and OUTR (8-bit), connected over a shared bus with a select line.
8-bit instructions: a 3-bit opcode and a 5-bit address into a 32-byte memory; the program is stored in ROM.
Hard-wired control: a sequence counter and decoders produce timing signals T0–T5 and opcode lines D0–D7, and gate logic turns them into register load, clear and increment signals.
ALU operations: add, subtract, signed compare (−1 / 0 / 1), shift left, complement, load, and an integer square root.
Verified in ModelSim by printing the memory contents after each instruction.

projects.title: Reliable Data Transfer over UDP
projects.summary: The Go-Back-N sliding-window protocol over a deliberately unreliable channel, with CRC error detection and Hamming codes.
projects.overview: UDP delivers packets without guarantees. This project rebuilds reliable, in-order delivery on top of it and tests it against a simulated bad network.
did: Python sender and receiver over UDP sockets: 3-bit sequence numbers, a window of four frames, cumulative ACKs, and a timeout that resends the whole window (Go-Back-N).
CRC with the generator 10011 to detect corrupted frames, and a Hamming code to detect and correct single-bit errors.
Fault injection: 20% packet loss, 20% lost ACKs and a 1% bit-error rate, to check that the message still arrives intact and in order.
Threads and a lock so that sending, receiving ACKs and timers run concurrently.

projects.title: Persian News Topic Classification
projects.summary: Classifying about 12,500 Persian news articles into six topics with an n-gram voting ensemble and a TF-IDF neural network.
projects.overview: News sites tag their articles with about 100 fine-grained labels. The task: predict an article's topic from its title and text.
did: Mapped the roughly 100 site tags onto six topics: social, economy, provinces, international, politics, and culture / sport / science.

Cleaned Persian text with Hazm (normalisation, tokenisation, stemming, stop-word removal) and stripped HTML entities, links and digits. Titles were given extra weight by repeating them before the body.
Soft-voting ensemble of SVM, XGBoost and Logistic Regression on 1–3-gram counts.
A second model: TF-IDF features (7,500 terms, 1–3-grams) feeding a small Keras MLP with dropout and early stopping.
results: On a held-out 20% split (2,083 articles): 84% accuracy and macro F1 0.82 for the voting ensemble.
85.1% accuracy (weighted F1 0.846) for the TF-IDF + MLP model.
Per-topic F1 ranged from 0.73 (culture, sport and science) to 0.88 (international).

projects.title: Course and Contest Platform in Java
projects.summary: A console platform for classrooms, exercises and timed contests, grown over three course projects to about 3,600 lines of object-oriented Java.
projects.overview: The main project of Advanced Programming: a Quera-style learning platform built in stages, where each new project extended the previous code base with new requirements.
did: Sign-up and log-in with validated email and national code, and different rights for admins, normal users and guests.

Classrooms, public or password-protected, with exercises built from four question types (fill-in-the-blank, descriptive, short answer, multiple choice) and four difficulty levels; multiple-choice answers are corrected automatically.
Timed contests in three kinds (normal, private, special) with groups, invitations and member limits.
Scoreboards for exercises and contests, exported as HTML tables.
Final stage: everything admins and users create is saved to files with Java serialization and loaded again on the next start.
Built with Maven, with Checkstyle and PMD tests required by the course.

projects.title: Computer Vision labs
projects.details: Thirteen weekly OpenCV labs: noise models and filtering, histograms and video, thresholding and morphology, template matching and edges, Hough transforms, geometric transformations, Harris and multiscale corners, SIFT matching and RANSAC alignment, and linear and logistic regression from scratch.

projects.title: Pitch and formants of my own voice
projects.course: Fundamentals of Speech and Language Processing
projects.details: I recorded a Persian sentence from Rabiner's speech-processing book in my own voice and wrote MATLAB code that extracts the pitch contour and the formants frame by frame using cepstral analysis.

projects.title: Line coding and audio coding
projects.details: Two signal-level projects. First, a bit stream sent as a polar signal through a channel with Gaussian noise, sampled at the middle of each bit, with the bit-error rate measured against signal voltage. Second, a recorded voice processed with amplification, μ-law and A-law companding, PCM and delta modulation.

projects.title: Linear algebra labs: face shapes and least squares
projects.details: Python labs applying linear algebra: images as matrices, solving systems and least squares on noisy measurements, and face-landmark analysis. Faces were aligned to a neutral face with affine registration, then SVD / PCA found the main modes of face-shape variation, animated one mode at a time.

projects.title: VHDL designs with testbenches
projects.details: VHDL designs simulated in ModelSim with their own testbenches, including a calculator that takes four 8-bit inputs and computes sums, means and variances of the odd and even values, and a counter.

projects.title: Genetic algorithm as hardware units in SystemC
projects.details: A genetic algorithm for a knapsack-style problem modelled in SystemC / C++ as separate hardware units: value and weight calculation, fitness evaluation, selection, crossover, mutation and population repair.

projects.title: AVR assembly programs
projects.details: Assembly programs for AVR microcontrollers, for example dividing a 16-bit number by an 8-bit number using only 8-bit registers.

projects.title: Linux kernel modules
projects.details: Loadable Linux kernel modules in C: load and unload hooks that log to the kernel log, and /proc entries that report the jiffies counter and the time elapsed since the module was loaded.

projects.title: Knights and Rogues: divide and conquer
projects.details: Among n knights, more than half are honest and the rest may answer anything. The task: identify the knights by asking them about each other. I designed a divide-and-conquer solution based on majority votes, implemented it in Python and explained it in a 10-page report.

projects.title: Command interpreter for typed arrays
projects.details: The first Advanced Programming project: a console program that reads commands to declare arrays of integers, doubles, characters or strings, assign values, change single members and run operations on whole arrays.

projects.title: Object-oriented Java homework
projects.details: Weekly assignments on object-oriented design: Death Arena (soldiers and guns with inheritance and a console graphics engine), a brick-breaker game model with several brick types, a hospital model, data-access objects that store people as JSON or plain text, and saving a binary search tree to a file.

projects.title: Data structures in Java
projects.details: Java assignments with written reports: converting infix and prefix expressions to postfix and evaluating them with stacks, a circular queue, and circular linked lists.
